players.product: AI / HPC data-center campuses on owned powered land (Hannibal campus with pending Long Ridge, Matagorda County TX; developed with Starwood) plus Exaion sovereign private cloud for AI inference in Europe

quarterly_data.signal: MARA 10-K capacity table: operational capacity of 1,315 MW and total capacity of 1,861 MW, of which owned sites 779 MW operational / 1,324 MW total (Central Texas 411 / 550 MW, East Ohio 79 / 225 MW, North Texas 78 / 180 MW, Central Ohio 28 / 150 MW, Central Nebraska 127 / 142 MW, International 57 / 77 MW) and hosted sites 536 MW operational / 537 MW total. Total energy capacity was 1.9 GW at December 31, 2025 (1.7 GW a year earlier).

quarterly_data.signal: MARA 10-K: 2025 revenues were $907,093 thousand versus $656,378 thousand in 2024, and MARA states its revenue is primarily derived from mining bitcoin; purchases of property and equipment were $407,071 thousand versus $250,825 thousand. MARA states its expansion into the AI and HPC industry is expected to increase capital intensity: AI and HPC data centers require substantial up-front capital expenditures, and hosting and leasing revenues generally materialize after construction completion and customer onboarding.
